An artificial fore-arm has a moment-of-inertia around the center of mass as 0.3kg.m2.

center of mass of the fore-arm is 20 cm, the moment-of-inertia of the fore-arm about
the elbow joint is ______ kg.m2. Give your answer rounded off to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IISc Bengaluru is 0.40 to 0.45.

questions.questionText:
A bio-potential signal of 4 mV on the skin surface was fed to an amplifier with a
differential gain of 2000. The noise in the signal is 1000 mV. If the amplifier output
produces a noise output of 200 mV, the common mode rejection ratio of the amplifier
is ______ dB. Give your answer rounded to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IISc Bengaluru is 80 to 80.

questions.questionText:
In a motor nerve conduction velocity experiment, the distance between the distal and
the recording sites is 4 cm and the distance between the proximal and the recording
sites is 24 cm. The distal and proximal latencies were recorded as 6 ms and 10 ms,
respectively. The nerve conduction velocity is _____ meters per second. Give your
answer rounded off to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IISc Bengaluru is 50 to 50.

questions.questionText:
A person creates an apparatus as shown in the figure to exercise the extensor muscle
of the hand. It is given that OP = 0.15 m, OQ = 0.35 m, 𝜃 = 30∘, the weight of the
lower arm = 20 N, the center of mass of the lower arm is at point P, the magnitude
of the applied tensile force F = 50 N. If the extensor muscle is acting with a moment
arm of 0.25 m, the muscle force required to hold the hand at the position shown in
the figure is _____ N. Give your answer rounded off to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IISc Bengaluru is 22 to 24.
